Why this exists

You already know the problem — you've been living it.

Every RMBN Money Market Fund notice, every weekly performance update, every factsheet — hand-built as one-off Outlook-safe HTML, one email at a time, with no system behind it. JARA is that system.

Today, without a system
  • Every template is hand-coded HTML, rebuilt from scratch or copy-pasted and hoped for the best
  • No visibility into whether an email actually reached the inbox, or landed in spam
  • Nothing stops a rushed send from going out with a broken layout or missing legal disclaimer
  • No record of who sent what, when, or who approved it
  • Personalization means manual mail-merge, or not doing it at all
With JARA
  • A real template library — reusable, versioned, and permanently on-brand
  • Genuine SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verification you can check any time, not a promise
  • A send is automatically blocked if it's missing an unsubscribe link or trips a spam-risk check
  • A complete, permanent audit trail of every action, by every person
  • Every recipient's name, account number, and details filled in automatically and safely
Inside the platform

What your team will actually sit down and use.

Nine screens, each doing one job well. Every screenshot below is the real product, not a mockup.

01 — Creation

Three on-brand templates from a paste or a PDF

Drop in a fund update, a policy notice, or an existing PDF, and the AI Template Studio returns three real, complete template options — already carrying RMB's logo, colours, and legal disclaimer. Nothing it produces can appear off-brand.

Every AI-composed template is checked against a fixed library of approved content blocks before it's ever shown — content the model invents outside that library is silently dropped, not displayed.
02 — Editing

A live editor anyone on the team can use

Edit real content in a split-view editor with an instant preview — no HTML, no code, no risk of breaking the layout. Brand elements like the logo, colour palette, and legal disclaimer are locked in place and simply cannot be removed by mistake.

03 — Library

Every approved template, in one place

The Template Bank replaces the folder of half-remembered .html files on someone's desktop. Every template is versioned, searchable, and ready to reuse — this month's factsheet email is next month's starting point, not a rebuild.

04 — Contacts

Real personalization, imported from Excel

Import your client list directly from Excel, organise it into groups — Institutional, Retail, High Net Worth — and attach custom fields like account number or relationship manager. Every email is personalized per recipient automatically.

If a template needs a recipient's first name and a contact record is missing one, the send is blocked for that recipient rather than going out with a broken placeholder — this exact scenario is tested before every release.
05 — Sending

A guided send, with a mandatory test first

A five-step wizard walks through template, personalization, recipients, and review — a test send is required before the real one is even offered. Content is automatically scanned for spam-risk language and missing unsubscribe links before it can go out.

06 — Oversight

Segregation of duties, built in

A Sender can build and test a campaign but cannot send it — it goes to an Admin for review first. The Admin sees exactly what the recipient will see before approving, and can send it back with a comment if anything needs to change.

07 — Proof

Real delivery data, not a guess

Sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced — tracked per campaign from real delivery events, not estimated. Alongside it, a genuine deliverability check of your sending domain's SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, so you know your emails are actually authenticated.

08 — Compliance

A permanent record, and a safety net for language

Every action — a send, an edit, an approval, a login — is written to a permanent audit log your compliance team can search and export. Outgoing content is also automatically checked for regulatory red-flag language, like promising a "guaranteed return," before it can be sent.

The part that matters most

A security model built for a regulated bank, not bolted on afterward.

Every claim below is a specific, real mechanism — not a marketing phrase. Where it's useful, we've named exactly how it works.

Five distinct access levels ENFORCED

Super Admin, Admin, Editor, Sender, and Viewer each have a precise, separate set of permissions. A Sender's account literally cannot reach user management or licence controls — not hidden, genuinely inaccessible, checked on every single action.

Cerebre cannot see your client data ARCHITECTURAL

Our own administrator accounts run in a completely separate part of the platform with no code path into your workspace. We can see that your licence is active — never your contacts, your templates, or a single word of your campaign content.

Cryptographically signed licensing Ed25519

Your annual licence is signed with the same class of cryptography used to secure SSH connections and the Signal messaging protocol. It's verified entirely offline, with no network round-trip — meaning it cannot be forged, even by someone intercepting your traffic.

A tampered licence — even a single altered character — is mathematically detectable and rejected before it's ever trusted.
Domain-level email authentication SPF · DKIM · DMARC

Every email is authenticated at the domain level, so your clients' own mail servers can cryptographically confirm a message genuinely came from RMB — not just that it claims to. This is checked live and shown honestly, not assumed.

Verified delivery event signatures HMAC

Delivery, open, and bounce data arrives through a channel that's cryptographically signature-checked against the exact reference values published by the industry's own webhook security standard — a malicious actor cannot fabricate a "delivered" status or forge suppression data.

A permanent, searchable audit trail RETAINED

Every send, edit, approval, login, and licence change is written permanently, with who, what, and when. Your compliance team gets a real, filterable interface — not a request to Cerebre's engineers for a database export.

Approval workflow before any send DUAL CONTROL

Content can be prepared by one person and must be formally signed off by another before it reaches a single client — the same segregation-of-duties principle your own internal processes already run on.

Automatic regulatory language check PRE-SEND

Outgoing content is automatically scanned for phrases that are real regulatory red flags for an asset manager — "guaranteed returns," "risk-free investment" — and blocked from sending until reworded. A second set of eyes your team doesn't have to remember to apply.

The deliverability screen — genuine SPF/DKIM/DMARC status, checked live, never simulated.
Licence status, verified offline — no dependency on Cerebre's servers being reachable.
The actual boundary

What Cerebre can see, and what it structurally cannot.

This isn't a policy promise — it's how the platform is built. Two genuinely separate parts of the system, with no shared code path between them.

Cerebre's view

  • Which workspaces exist
  • Licence tier and expiry
  • Whether a workspace is active
  • Nothing about what's inside it
NO ACCESS

RMB's workspace

  • Every client contact and their details
  • Every template and its content
  • Every campaign, sent or scheduled
  • Your own team's full audit history
Direct answers

The questions your team will actually ask.

In a dedicated Postgres database, with every single query scoped to RMB's own workspace ID at the code level — there is no query path in the application that can return another workspace's data into your view. This isn't a filter applied after the fact; it's how every screen is built.
No. Cerebre's administrator accounts run in a physically separate part of the application — a different login area, a different set of screens — that has no code path into any workspace's contacts, templates, or campaign content. What Cerebre can see is account-level only: that your workspace exists, your licence tier, and whether it's active.
You move into a grace period first, with clear renewal reminders in-app — nothing is deleted and nothing stops working immediately. If it lapses fully, sending pauses until renewed, but your contacts, templates, and history remain exactly as they were. Renewal itself is a code you paste in and activate yourselves, verified instantly and entirely offline.
Yes, in two layers. Role permissions control who can even open the Send Centre. On top of that, the approval workflow means most roles can prepare a campaign but not actually send it — it goes to an Admin for review first, who sees exactly what a recipient would see before approving.
Your sending domain is authenticated with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC — the same domain-level checks banks and major platforms rely on. This means a recipient's own mail server can cryptographically verify the email genuinely originated from RMB's authorized infrastructure. JARA shows you this status live, not as a one-time setup claim.
Three independent layers: a mandatory test send before any real one is offered, an automatic scan for regulatory red-flag language like "guaranteed returns" that blocks sending until reworded, and the approval workflow requiring a second person's sign-off. None of these rely on someone remembering to check.
The licensing model is explicitly built for that. Verification happens fully offline using a public key already built into the application — a self-hosted deployment can validate its own licence without ever contacting Cerebre's servers. It's designed as a genuine option, not a hypothetical.
Yes — a permanent, searchable audit log covering sends, edits, approvals, logins, and licence changes, each tied to the specific person and timestamp. It has its own interface for your compliance team to search and export directly, with a configurable retention policy rather than an indefinite or arbitrary one.
